extensions.platform: Native desktop Pygame. Canonical values are RGB tuples in config.py (tampilan.py and main.py still hold a few component literals: Muted Tarp, Field Rim, Night Shadow, Letterbox); hex here is an exact conversion.

display.purpose: Stall name sign and winner sign; steps to 40px then 28px when a winner name would not fit.

headline.purpose: Screen titles on cream boards, KUIS plaque, rosette numeral.

numeral.purpose: Ranking positions on the winner table.

label.purpose: Tile numbers, MULAI and FINIS tile words, panel titles (PAPAN SKOR · <KESULITAN>), toggles, form labels, sound pill, answer letters, timer digits, log serials, marker digits, score pops, dialog titles.

question.purpose: Question text, two lines; longer questions drop to Body Strong, three lines max.

body.purpose: Rules text on the how-to-play board, 26px pitch, 560px measure.

body-strong.purpose: Menu tagline, name fields, ranking names, legend headings.

small.purpose: Helper text (difficulty summary, question count), score lines, log lines, footer, dialog body.

small-strong.purpose: Answer text, scoreboard names, the question status line (<kategori> · <materi>), errors, newest log line.

shadows.name: plank
shadows.purpose: Every painted board and button at rest (bayangan default: offset 0,6, blur 10, alpha 90).

shadows.name: floor
shadows.value: ellipse (2 x token radius) x 10px rgba(0, 0, 0, 0.27)
shadows.purpose: Under every token; narrows as the token lifts.

shadows.name: modal-dim
shadows.purpose: Full-canvas dim behind the exit confirmation (alpha 160).

shadows.name: route-dim
shadows.purpose: Off-route tiles while a token moves (alpha 55).

shadows.name: paint-gloss
shadows.value: 3px strip, fill lightened 22%, inset radius/2 from the sides, 3px from top
shadows.purpose: Gloss line on every painted board.

shadows.name: paint-rim
shadows.value: 3px stroke, fill darkened 35% (4px on the big signs)
shadows.purpose: Hand-painted rim on every painted board.

motion.name: ease-out-cubic
motion.purpose: The single easing curve for slides, tumbles, hops and transits.

motion.name: card-slide
motion.purpose: New question slides in like a ticket pushed under the booth window.

motion.name: dice-tumble
motion.value: 0.8s, 540deg rotation easing to 0, face changes every 0.07s

motion.name: token-hop
motion.purpose: Token hops tile by tile with a step sound.

motion.name: prop-transit
motion.purpose: Token rides a ladder up or a snake down.

motion.name: route-light
motion.purpose: Signature: bulbs light ahead of the token.

motion.name: bulb-idle-frame
motion.purpose: Board frame bulbs, mostly dark with a slow sweep.

motion.name: bulb-active-ring
motion.purpose: Eight bulbs around the active player's tile.

motion.name: bulb-all
motion.purpose: Winner screen string, the prize moment.

motion.name: score-count
motion.value: lerp toward target at rate dt * 8
motion.purpose: Scoreboard numbers count rather than jump.

motion.name: hover-lift
motion.purpose: Hover on planks and answer options; disabled on touch.

motion.name: result-hold
motion.purpose: Answer result stays before the turn moves on (bot thinking also 1.5s; bot roll 0.9s; winner screen after 1.4s).

breakpoints.name: canvas
breakpoints.value: 1280x720 logical, scaled uniformly to the window and letterboxed; no reflow

board.grid: 8x8 = 64 tiles of 78px (624px square) at (30, 48), zig-zag from 1 bottom left to 64 top left; 18px bulb frame, 660px outer.
board.props: Snake body thickness 10 (menu 17, legend 9), tapering to 38%; ladder rails 22px apart, rungs every 18px, 12px overhang past tile centres.

narrative.overview:
The whole game is a night-market game stall. The ground is a deep terpal-blue tent with stitched seams and soft folds; everything the player touches sits on top of it as a plywood board painted in flat sign-painter colours (red, yellow, cream, green) with a darker hand-painted rim and a thin gloss line along the top. Light is the stall's currency: strings of bulbs hang across the tent and frame the board, and heat is rationed. Most bulbs idle dim; the active player's tile, the route ahead of a moving token, and the winner's moment burn full.

The board is a lit stall table of 64 painted tiles (8x8), the question is a cream card at the ticket booth, the dice are thrown on the counter, the game log is a stack of paper karcis with a perforated stub and serial numbers. Snakes and ladders are painted props, drawn from primitives rather than imported art: a tapering purple snake with yellow bands and a forked red tongue, a wooden ladder with dark-edged rungs. Three difficulty levels (Mudah, Sedang, Sulit) change how many props stand on the table, never how they are painted. Signs speak in Bungee, a chunky sign-painter display face; questions, answers and data speak in Atkinson Hyperlegible so a student reads them at a glance.

The canvas is a fixed 1280x720 stage, scaled whole to the window. Density is moderate and game-like: one board on the left, one stacked column of painted planks on the right. The world refuses the cartoon jungle board and the dark neon gamer HUD.
keyCharacteristics: Terpal-blue tent ground, never a flat fill: alternating 214px panels, central fold shading, dashed seam stitches, a darkened ground band at the bottom.
Every surface is a painted plank: flat fill, 3px darker rim, 3px gloss strip, soft blurred drop shadow.
Bulbs as the light and state system, with lit, idle and dead states.
Bungee for signs, labels and numerals; Atkinson Hyperlegible for anything to be read.
Players are a colour plus a number, always together.
Motion is physical and eased: cards slide in, dice tumble, tokens hop, bulbs warm and cool.
Difficulty changes the count of props and the bot's accuracy; the paint, sizes and layout stay the same.

rules.name: The Rationed Heat Rule
rules.body: Only three things burn bulbs at full: the eight-bulb ring around the active player's tile, the bulbs on the route ahead of a moving token, and the winner screen's string. Frame bulbs idle at most 0.55 heat with a slow sweep; the menu string chases. If everything is lit, nothing is.

rules.name: The Cream Reads Rule
rules.body: Anything meant to be read at length (a question, a rule, a log line) sits on Cream or Dark Cream in Ink. Red, yellow and green planks carry short sign words only.

rules.name: The Colour Plus Number Rule
rules.body: A player is never identified by colour alone; every token carries its player number in Bungee, Ink on Kuning, Cream on the other three.

rules.name: The 18px Floor Rule
rules.body: No text renders below 18px on the 1280x720 canvas. Shrink by stepping down the ramp, never by inventing a size.

rules.name: The Sign and Card Rule
rules.body: Bungee is never used for a sentence; Atkinson is never used for a sign word. Headings, buttons, labels and numerals are Bungee; anything with a verb in it is Atkinson.

rules.name: The Lift Means Live Rule
rules.body: Raised means interactive or current: hovered planks rise 2px, the active scoreboard row rises 3px, a moving token lifts in an arc. Spent things lose their shadow and sit flat.

dos: Do draw every surface with the painted-board treatment: flat fill, 3px gloss strip lightened 22%, rim darkened 35%, Plank shadow.
Do put the tent behind every screen, panels and seams included; never a flat blue fill.
Do ration bulb heat: full burn only for the active tile ring, the moving route, and the winner screen.
Do keep a player's colour and number together on every token, in every list.
Do use Bungee for signs, labels and numerals and Atkinson Hyperlegible for questions, answers, names and sentences, at 18px or larger.
Do state why a button is disabled in its own label.
Do ease motion out (cubic) and make game events visible: tumble, hop, slide, count, pop.
Do let difficulty change only the rules (prop count, bot accuracy) and name it where the game is played (the score header).
Do add new colour values to config.py and draw props with primitives; no external art.
donts: Don't use hard, unblurred offset shadows; shadows are soft and fall straight down.
Don't light every bulb outside the winner screen.
Don't identify a player by colour alone.
Don't set a sentence in Bungee or a sign word in Atkinson.
Don't reuse player colours, Snake Purple or Ladder Green for unrelated UI.
Don't give a difficulty level its own palette, tile size or prop style.
Don't reflow the layout per window size; scale the 1280x720 stage whole.
Don't drift toward a cartoon jungle board or a dark neon gamer HUD.
